name: Direct play
description: Makes your films and series play directly on the devices you choose, so Jellyfin does not convert them as they play: one file at a time, in the hours you choose.
author: TheMightyTRexUK

settings.label: Roku Express and older Rokus
settings.hint: H.264 up to 1080p; Dolby Digital, AAC and MP3 sound. No HEVC, DTS or TrueHD.

settings.label: Roku 4K
settings.hint: Roku Express 4K, Streaming Stick 4K and Ultra: H.264 and HEVC up to 4K. No DTS or TrueHD.

settings.label: Fire TV Sticks
settings.hint: H.264 and HEVC up to 1080p, so the HD sticks play them too. No DTS or TrueHD.

settings.label: Chromecast
settings.hint: H.264 up to 1080p; AAC, MP3, Opus and FLAC sound. No HEVC, Dolby Digital, DTS or TrueHD.

settings.label: Smart TV apps
settings.hint: Jellyfin on Samsung and LG televisions: H.264 and HEVC up to 4K. No DTS or TrueHD.

settings.label: Web browsers
settings.hint: H.264 up to 4K; AAC, MP3, Opus and FLAC sound. No HEVC or Dolby Digital, so files with only Dolby Digital get a stereo track.

settings.label: Apple TV
settings.hint: H.264 and HEVC up to 4K; Dolby Digital, AAC and FLAC sound. No DTS or TrueHD.

settings.label: Nvidia Shield
settings.hint: Nearly everything, DTS and TrueHD included, up to 4K.

settings.label: When it works
settings.hint: One file at a time, at the lowest priority. The file being converted always finishes.

settings.label: Shrink very large H.264 files
settings.hint: Converts H.264 files with a higher bitrate than below again, at the same picture quality. A file is kept as it was when it would not get at least a tenth smaller.

settings.label: Convert HEVC to H.264
settings.hint: Only when none of your devices plays HEVC. H.264 files are larger, so this uses more space.

settings.label: Keep the originals
settings.hint: Moves each original to a .direct-play-originals folder in movies or tv instead of replacing it, so you can delete them yourself. Saves no space until you do.

settings.label: Card updates every
settings.hint: How often the Direct play card on the dashboard shows the progress while a file is converted.

changed: **Lighter at rest:** it wakes about once a minute while nothing asks it anything, not twice a second; its minute's look for work reads its settings once, not about ninety times; and it writes nothing to its folder when a run goes well.
**Starts faster:** its image comes with Python's modules already compiled, so a start takes about a quarter of the processor time.

**Lighter dashboard card:** the cards and the minute's look for work no longer read every file's details each time; with 50,000 files the card answers in about 4 ms instead of 230 ms, and about 45 MB less memory is held.

added: **Plays directly on the devices you choose:** Rokus, Fire TV Sticks, Chromecast, smart TV apps, web browsers, Apple TV and Nvidia Shield
**Four fixes, cheapest first:** repackages the wrong container, adds a sound track your devices play beside the original, shrinks very large H.264 files and converts old formats to H.264
**Checked before it replaces:** the length, the picture, the first sound track and where sound and picture start; a file that fails is left as it was
**One file at a time, at the lowest priority:** at weekends, in quiet hours or any time, with Pause and Resume
**On the dashboard:** what is being converted, what is next and how much space it has saved
**A logo and a status on its cards:** the grey band at the top of each card says whether it is converting, waiting, paused or done, and when it last changed.
**Updates safely:** before an update it stops the file being converted, which is converted again afterwards, and starts no new one.
